content: Migration of your Thunderbird data from the old Mac to the new Mac can be done with simple copy and drag & drop actions. On your old Mac copy the entire folder "Thunderbird" from your user Library on an external hard drive with at least 250 GB memory. Plug the external HD to your new Mac, verify that Thunderbird is not running, open a Finder window, select your user Library and drag & drop the Thunderbird folder in your user Library. If you have already run Thunderbird on the new Mac the system will ask you to replace the already existing Thunderbird folder.

content:
Thunderbird does not have "an account" as is the case with many mail clients, it has incoming accounts and outgoing accounts and they are linked via the identity information on the incoming account (there is also no limit on the number of distinct identities you can have on and incoming account.)

I therefore really do not follow your line of thought. There is no limit to the number of SMTP servers that can be configured and each can have it's own used name and password. The SMTP to be used with an identity is set in the account settings for the incoming account on the identity pane (the one above server settings)

Check the outgoing server(SMTP) entry in account settings for configured outgoing servers and add whatever you need.

content: Hila, El error de extensión no permitida no viene de Mozilla Thunderbird, sino del servidor de correo saliente (SMTP) que usas. Por seguridad, muchos servidores bloquean el envío de archivos .eml porque pueden contener código ejecutable. La solución rápida es comprimir el archivo en un formato ZIP antes de adjuntarlo o cambiarle la extensión a .dat e informar en el texto del correo. Saludos
